verdict.rationale: Modal's own docs show GPU selection per Function via the `gpu` argument, deployment of serverless applications through the Python SDK, and endpoints that scale with traffic and idle at zero. Containers spin up and down in 1-2 seconds, and users never pay for idle resources, which directly replaces always-on instances. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of scale-to-zero GPU behavior, and documentation of autoscaler configuration such as min/max containers and scaledown timing.

support.subject: As a developer, I can deploy code to autoscaling serverless GPU workers that scale to zero, instead of managing always-on instances

citations.quote: You can pick a specific GPU type for your Function via the `gpu` argument.
Turn any function into an HTTPS endpoint that scales with traffic and idles at zero.
You never pay for idle resources — just actual compute time, by the CPU cycle.
In contrast, _Modal spins containers_ up and down in 1-2 seconds.
The [Modal](https://modal.com/) Python SDK allows you to deploy high-performance serverless applications and programmatically interact with the Modal platform.
